x.t: Helpers get ready as a storm heads towards India's coast
b: India's [[imd|weather office]] is watching a storm at sea. It is expected to become a [[cyclone|cyclone]] on Monday evening. Then it will be called Akvan.
It should reach the coast of [[andhra-pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] on Friday. That gives four days to get ready.
Fishermen were told to stay on shore to keep safe. Rescue teams in Odisha are ready to help. Families should follow official updates, because forecasts can change.

o.t: Storm expected to reach Andhra coast on Friday as states get ready
b: India's weather office, the [[imd|IMD]], expects a storm over the [[bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]] to reach the [[andhra-pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] coast between Nellore and Tuni by about noon on Friday 20 November. That gives four days of warning.

On Monday it was a deep [[depression|depression]], a strong area of low air pressure with wind and rain. It was expected to become a [[cyclone|cyclonic storm]], a stronger spinning storm, that evening, and be named Akvan. It should reach land as a very severe cyclonic storm, with winds of 120 to 130 kilometres an hour and gusts, or sudden bursts, of up to 145 kilometres an hour.

Fishermen have been told not to go to sea, to keep safe. Odisha has 24-hour control rooms and rescue teams on standby. Andhra Pradesh's Chief Minister, N Chandrababu Naidu, the head of the state government, told officials to take safety measures early. People are urged to follow official updates.

stories.think: If your family had four days to get ready for a big storm, what would you do first, and why?

quiz.q: On which day is the storm expected to reach the coast?

x.t: Scientists count about 382 rare right whales
b: North Atlantic right whales are rare. Scientists count them each year to see how they are doing. In 2025, there were about 382.
That is slightly fewer than the year before. The whales can get tangled in fishing gear. Ships can also hit them.
There is good news too. In the latest season, 24 baby whales, called [[calf|calves]], were born. That is one of the best seasons on record.

o.t: Rare right whale count falls to about 382, but calves bring hope
b: There were about 382 North Atlantic right whales in 2025, about 2% fewer than the year before, says a yearly estimate released on Monday 16 November. It comes from the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium, a group of US and Canadian scientists and organisations that study and protect the whales.

The whales give birth in winter off the south-east US and feed off New England and Canada. They eat [[copepod|copepods]], tiny sea animals. [[whaling|Whaling]], or hunting whales, made them very rare, until hunting them mostly stopped in the 1930s. Today the main dangers are getting tangled in fishing gear and being hit by ships. Warming water has moved their food, so whales go where there are fewer protections.
The hopeful news: 24 [[calf|calves]] were born in the 2025 to 2026 calving season, one of the best on record. The consortium meets in Nova Scotia this week.

stories.think: When there are only a few hundred of an animal left, why might every single one matter?

quiz.q: About how many North Atlantic right whales were there in 2025?

x.t: Cricket's big contests in India now have dates
b: The [[icc|ICC]] runs world cricket. Its leaders met in Bali, Indonesia, to plan ahead.

They set dates for two big men's contests in India. The Champions Trophy starts on 9 October 2029. India will share the World Cup with Bangladesh. It starts on 9 October 2031. India was picked to host both in 2021.
Jay Shah, from India, will lead the ICC again. No one stood against him.

o.t: Dates set for India's 2029 and 2031 cricket events; Shah stays chair
b: The [[icc|International Cricket Council (ICC)]], which runs world cricket, held board meetings in Bali, Indonesia. On Sunday 15 November the board set dates for its men's tournaments up to 2035. India will host the Champions Trophy from 9 to 28 October 2029. India and Bangladesh will host the Men's Cricket World Cup, played as [[odi|one-day internationals]], from 9 October to 23 November 2031.

The hosts were first chosen in 2021; the news is the dates. On Monday 16 November the ICC said Jay Shah of India had been reappointed as its [[chair|chair]], or leader, for a second term. He was unopposed: no one stood against him.

Cricket returns at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. Two qualifying events, which decide who gets a place, are set for early 2028: the men's in Bangladesh and the women's in the USA. Only the winner of each goes to Los Angeles.

stories.think: Why might sports organisers want to fix the dates of big contests years ahead?

x.t: A new promise aims to make AI kinder to the planet
b: [[ai|AI]] apps run on big computers that use lots of electricity and water.

On Monday, a climate meeting called [[cop|COP31]] launched a new promise. It asks people to use AI to fight [[climate-change|climate change]]. It also asks AI computers to use clean power, to harm the planet less.
Nobody has to sign it. Only a few countries have signed. They will check how they are doing next year.

o.t: Climate talks launch a voluntary pledge to make AI greener
b: The Antalya AI Pledge was launched on Monday 16 November at [[cop|COP31]], the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye. Türkiye developed it with the [[itu|ITU]], the UN agency for digital technology. Signing is voluntary, or optional.

[[ai|AI]], or artificial intelligence, runs on computers that use lots of electricity and water. The pledge aims to use AI to fight [[climate-change|climate change]] while shrinking AI's own harm to the planet. It asks for clean power for AI computers and data centres, the buildings that hold them, and for measuring and reporting AI's effect on the environment.

Signers will first check progress together at next year's COP in Ethiopia. Support so far is limited. A first draft, or first full version, of the summit's main agreement was due early this week, and countries still disagree on new energy targets. Talks are due to end on Friday 20 November.

stories.think: Every app and game runs on real computers that use energy. Should people think about that when they use them? Why or why not?

quiz.q: What do the computers behind AI use a lot of?

x.t: A tennis player tries again and gets his first win
b: Only eight of the season's best men's tennis players get into the [[atp-finals|ATP Finals]]. They play in two groups of four. It is in [[turin|Turin]], Italy.
Ben Shelton from the USA first played here last year. He lost all his group matches. On Sunday he beat Arthur Fils from France. It was his first win here.
World number one Alexander Zverev also won. The final is on 22 November.

o.t: Shelton earns first ATP Finals win; world No. 1 Zverev also wins
b: The [[atp-finals|ATP Finals]] began in Turin, Italy, on Sunday 15 November. World number one Alexander Zverev of Germany beat Spain's Rafael Jodar in two [[set|sets]], 6-4, 6-4. A set is one part of a tennis match.
Later, Ben Shelton of the USA beat France's Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3. It was his first win at the ATP Finals. When he first played at the event last year, he lost all his group matches.

Only eight of the season's best singles players qualify. They are split into two groups of four, and in this [[round-robin|round-robin]] format each player plays the other three in the group. The top two in each group reach the semi-finals, the round before the final. The final is on Sunday 22 November. Shelton plays Zverev on Tuesday.

x.t: Prices that businesses pay for goods go up faster
b: Businesses sell goods to each other in big amounts. The price they pay is called the [[wholesale|wholesale]] price. It is not the price you pay in a shop.
In October, India's wholesale prices were 12.29% higher than a year before. That rise is bigger than in September.
Fuel and power prices went up the most. The government said oil, gas, metals and some foods also pushed prices up.

o.t: Wholesale prices rise faster in October, pushed by fuel and power
b: India's [[wpi|Wholesale Price Index]] (WPI) rose 12.29% in October compared with a year earlier, up from 11.39% in September, figures from the Ministry of Commerce and Industry showed on Monday 16 November. The WPI tracks the average change in prices of goods sold in bulk, or large amounts, between businesses. These are called [[wholesale|wholesale]] prices.

The biggest rise was in fuel and power, at 32.84%, up from 25.85% in September. The ministry said higher prices for oil, gas, electricity, basic metals, chemicals and food products pushed [[inflation|inflation]], the rise in prices over time, up.

Wholesale prices are different from retail prices, the prices shoppers pay in shops. Retail inflation was 6.09% in October, above the 6% upper limit set for the [[rbi|Reserve Bank of India]]. The WPI is published by the ministry's Office of the Economic Adviser.

x.t: Indonesia says sorry to its neighbours for wildfire smoke
b: Smoke can drift from one country to another. Wildfires in Indonesia burned for months. The smoke reached Singapore and Malaysia.
On Sunday, Indonesia's leader said sorry to them for the smoke. He spoke at a meeting of [[asean|Southeast Asian]] leaders.
Indonesia sent 71,000 firefighters to fight the fires. It also plans a new team to stop fires before they start.

o.t: Indonesia says sorry for wildfire haze and turns to prevention
b: Smoke does not stop at borders. Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto apologised to Singapore and Malaysia for [[haze|haze]], smoky air, from months of wildfires in Indonesia. He spoke on Sunday 15 November at the 49th [[asean|ASEAN]] Summit in Manila, a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. The fires burned mainly on Sumatra, Borneo and Papua.

Prabowo said Indonesia had deployed 71,000 firefighters. The government has also revoked, or cancelled, 17 land permits held by companies, and 26 more companies are being investigated. Indonesia says it will keep taking firm action against companies linked to the fires.
Indonesia is also preparing a new agency to strengthen wildfire prevention, which means stopping fires before they start.

stories.think: If something from your home bothered your neighbours by accident, what would you do to make it right?

quiz.q: How many firefighters did Indonesia send to fight the fires?

x.t: A special day for news, and the group that keeps it fair
b: Every year on 16 November, India marks National Press Day. The press means newspapers and reporters. On this day in 1966, the [[press-council|Press Council of India]] began work. That was 60 years ago.
The Press Council is like a referee for news. It looks into complaints to keep reporting fair.
It also stands up for [[press-freedom|reporters' freedom]] to share the news.

o.t: National Press Day: 60 years of the Press Council of India
b: India marks National Press Day every year on 16 November. It is the date the [[press-council|Press Council of India]] (PCI) began functioning, or started work, in 1966. This year marks 60 years since then.

The PCI is an independent body. Its job is to make sure the press, meaning newspapers and journalists, keeps high standards and reports honestly and fairly. It examines complaints that journalists have broken the rules of good reporting. It also works to protect [[press-freedom|press freedom]], the freedom of journalists to report without outside interference.
This year's theme is "Journalism: Populist or Responsible". It asks whether news should chase what is popular or be responsible.

stories.think: If a friend tells you a surprising piece of news, how could you check whether it is true?

quiz.q: In which year did the Press Council of India begin its work?

in-akvan.ctx: On 16 November the IMD said the storm should cross the coast between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Friday; landfall is when a storm's centre crosses the coast. Storm names come from a list kept by the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones, with 13 countries contributing names that are used in a fixed order, and Akvan was contributed by Iran. This would be Andhra Pradesh's third cyclone in less than a month, after Arnab and Murasu.
in-akvan.ask: Fishermen were told to stay ashore days before the storm is due, even though forecasts can change: is it better to warn people early, or to wait until a forecast is more certain?

g-right-whales.ctx: AP reports that the population fell by about a quarter between 2010 and 2020. Only about 73 of the whales are breeding females, and three of the mothers in the latest calving season were having a calf for the first time. Scientists from the New England Aquarium help work out the estimate each year.
g-right-whales.ask: Fishing crews and ships work in the same waters where right whales live: how should people balance fishing jobs with protecting a whale this rare?

in-icc.ctx: The ICC also set dates for other men's events, including the 2028 men's T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand, from 12 October to 12 November 2028. Each Olympic qualifier will have eight teams in two groups of four, and the two group winners will play a final for the one place at Los Angeles 2028. Shah has been ICC chair since 2024 and was formerly secretary of India's cricket board, the BCCI.

g-ai-pledge.ctx: The COP31 presidency's website says the pledge was first announced in New York in September. The ITU says it was formally launched on Monday at a COP31 meeting on AI. The ITU says signers choose at least one of four kinds of commitment, which also include designing and buying AI responsibly, and money and technical help so developing countries can use AI for climate action.
g-ai-pledge.ask: Supporters say a voluntary pledge starts shared action, while critics say promises without firm checks may be too vague: is a voluntary promise a good first step, or should limits on AI's harm to the planet be required?

in-wpi.ctx: The government says the current WPI series, released on 15 June 2026, uses 2022-23 as its base year in place of 2011-12. It says manufactured products make up about 63% of the index, primary articles about 23% and fuel and power about 14%. Business Standard reports that Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, said companies have passed on only a limited part of the input cost increase to consumers.
in-wpi.ask: When the cost of fuel and electricity rises, should businesses pass the extra cost on to shoppers straight away, or absorb some of it for a while?

g-haze.ask: When smoke from one country's fires reaches its neighbours, should that country carry the main responsibility, or should the whole region share the work of stopping it?

imd: India's weather office. It watches the weather and warns people about storms.
The India Meteorological Department, India's weather office. It forecasts the weather, tracks storms and names cyclones over the north Indian Ocean.
cyclone: A big spinning storm. It forms over the sea and brings strong wind and rain.
A large storm that forms over the sea, with strong winds turning around a centre. India's weather office calls a system a cyclonic storm when its winds reach 62 kilometres an hour.
andhra-pradesh: A state in India. It has a coast on the Bay of Bengal.
A state in India with a coast on the Bay of Bengal.
bay-of-bengal: A big part of the sea to the east of India.
A large part of the north Indian Ocean, to the east of India. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have coasts on it.
depression: In weather, a patch of low air pressure with wind and rain. It is weaker than a cyclone.
In weather, an area of low air pressure that brings wind and rain. Over the sea, a depression can strengthen into a cyclonic storm.
press-council: A group that helps keep news in India honest and fair. It is like a referee for news.

An independent body that works to keep India's press to high standards of journalism, examines complaints about breaking the rules of good reporting, and protects press freedom. It began functioning on 16 November 1966.
press-freedom: The freedom of reporters to tell people the news.
The freedom of newspapers and journalists to report the news without outside interference.
wholesale: Selling goods in big amounts to businesses, not to shoppers.
The sale of goods in bulk, or large amounts, between businesses, before the goods reach shoppers.
wpi: A number that shows how fast the prices of goods sold in big amounts are changing.
India's monthly measure of the average change in prices of goods sold in bulk between businesses. It is published by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
inflation: When prices in the shops keep going up.
A rise in prices over time. It is usually given as a percentage: how much more things cost than a year ago.
rbi: India's central bank. It looks after the country's money.
India's central bank. Its target is to keep inflation at 4 per cent, within a band of 2 to 6 per cent, and it sets a main interest rate.
ai: Artificial intelligence: computer programs that can learn and make choices.
Artificial intelligence: computer systems that learn patterns from data to recognise images, understand language or make predictions.
cop: A big meeting where countries talk about climate change.
Short for Conference of the Parties: the United Nations climate summit, where countries meet to agree on action on climate change.
climate-change: Earth is slowly getting warmer, and the weather is changing with it.
The long-term warming of the Earth and the changes in weather that come with it. Burning fossil fuels is the main cause.
itu: A part of the United Nations that works on phones, the internet and other digital technology.
The International Telecommunication Union, the United Nations agency for digital technology. It worked with Türkiye on the Antalya AI Pledge.
asean: A group of countries in Southeast Asia that work together.
Short for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, a group of countries in Southeast Asia that cooperate on trade, safety and other shared issues.
haze: Smoke or dust in the air that makes it look cloudy and hard to see far.
Smoke, dust or other tiny particles in the air that make it look cloudy. Smoke haze from big wildfires can drift across borders to other countries.
copepod: A tiny sea animal. Right whales eat lots of them.
A tiny crustacean, a small animal with a hard outer shell, that lives in the sea. Copepods are the main food of North Atlantic right whales.
calf: A young whale. Right whale mothers give birth to their calves in winter.
whaling: The hunting of whales. Whaling made North Atlantic right whales very rare, until hunting them mostly stopped in the 1930s.
icc: The group that runs world cricket and plans its big contests.
The International Cricket Council, the body that runs world cricket. Its board chooses the hosts and dates of world tournaments.
odi: A cricket match between countries that is played in one day.
One Day International: a cricket match between countries in which each team bats for up to 50 overs.
chair: The person who leads a group and its meetings.
The person who leads an organisation's board and runs its meetings.
atp-finals: A tennis contest at the end of the year for eight of the best men's players.
The tournament that ends the men's tennis season. Eight of the season's best singles players qualify and play in two groups of four.
turin: A city in Italy where the ATP Finals are being played.
set: One part of a tennis match.
One part of a tennis match, made up of games. Players have to win sets to win the match.
round-robin: A contest where everyone in a group plays everyone else.
A format in which every player or team in a group plays all the others, with no instant knockout.
light-day: How far light travels in one whole day. It is a very long way.
A unit of distance: how far light travels in 24 hours, about 25.9 billion kilometres.
deep-space-network: The system NASA uses to talk to faraway spacecraft.
NASA's system for communicating with distant spacecraft such as Voyager 1. It is managed by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
orbit: The path something follows as it goes round and round a planet, moon or star.
The curved path an object follows around a planet, moon or star, held there by gravity.
interstellar: Space beyond the heliopause, the place where the Sun's constant flow of material and its magnetic field stop affecting their surroundings.
jpl: A NASA centre in California. The Voyager 1 mission is run from there.
A NASA laboratory in Pasadena, California. The Voyager mission is run from there.

o.t: What is a light-year, and how fast is light?
b: In empty space, light travels at 299,792,458 metres per second. That is about 300,000 kilometres every second.

Distances in space are so large that astronomers measure them by how far light travels. A light-year is the distance light travels in one year: about 9.46 trillion kilometres. It is a unit of distance, not of time.

The Sun is about 150 million kilometres from Earth, and NASA says its light takes about 8.3 minutes to reach us. The nearest star beyond the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is a little more than 4 light-years away. A light-day, the distance Voyager 1 reaches this week, is how far light travels in 24 hours: about 25.9 billion kilometres.

backThen.t: A radio message is beamed from Earth towards the stars
backThen.o: On 16 November 1974, a radio message was sent into space from the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. It was sent during a ceremony to mark a major upgrade to the observatory's radio telescope. A team that included the astronomers Frank Drake and Carl Sagan created it. The message included a simple picture of a human and a diagram of the solar system. It was aimed at M13, a cluster of stars more than 20,000 light-years away.
backThen.x: On this day in 1974, scientists sent a radio message into space. They sent it from the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. The message had a simple picture of a person in it.
backThen.why: A radio message travels at the speed of light. A light-year is how far light travels in one year, so the message needs more than 20,000 years to reach those stars. That shows how big space is.

hiddenWords.o: Orbit comes from the Latin word orbita, which means a track or rut, such as the track left by a wheel.
Cyclone comes from Greek words about going around in a circle. It is linked to the Greek word kyklos, which means a circle.
